# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete – Updated 89)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; **spring of third year (present narrative through auction, financial crisis, and engagement rupture)**; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Harrowgate, parsonage, forge, Brompton, barracks neighbourhood, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange, Russell Square, Coldcombe hill farms, Salford granary, Champ de Mars (France)

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist
- **Secret Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rawdon in Brompton lodgings; wearing new gloves, shawls, rings, watch purchased by Rawdon; marriage revealed through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs; denied access to Miss Crawley at Park Lane; letters sent back unopened

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license
- **Current Status**: Living with Rebecca in Brompton lodgings furnished luxuriously; awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; anxiously considers possibility she may not recover (potential loss of fifty thousand pounds inheritance); denied door access by Mr. Bowls at Park Lane; servants cannot gain lodgment; letters unopened; financial strain evident
- **Debt**: Won two hundred pounds from George Osborne at billiards at Cocoa-Tree

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute Crawley's continuous nursing; month elapsed; not "coming-to"; never stirs out; unwell; door kept by Mr. Bowls; access denied to Rawdon and Rebecca; letters unopened

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; arrived at Park Lane morning of marriage revelation crisis; declared Rebecca "artful little hussy"; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley; took vacant room at Park Lane; remains continuously present; guards access; has not left her side

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul; confirmed engagement to George; completely innocent of broader events initially
- **Emotional and Financial Crisis**: Father ruined; family thrust into poverty; lying awake unhappy overhead during family crisis; ailing and low-spirited; isolated despite family presence; no true confidante; secretly harbors doubts about George's faithfulness and neglect
- **Heartbreak**: Father John Sedley cursed Osborne family as heartless, wicked, ungrateful and ordered Emmy to banish George from her mind and return presents and letters; she promised acquiescence but could not part with letters—placed them back in bosom, unable to live without this consolation; brooded over letters constantly, living in past life; each letter recalled circumstances; these relics were all she had left; business of her life became to watch the corpse of Love; looked to death with inexpressible longing, thinking she could follow George then
- **Engagement Rupture**: Engagement to George broken off by John Osborne's veto; her happiness and character compromised; society now judges her as criminal and imprudent (per Mrs. Smith and Mrs. Brown); Misses Dobbin declare "Captain Osborne, of course, could not marry a bankrupt's daughter"; peers consider her folly and familiarities horrid and inappropriate; faces reputation damage and isolation

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant now ruined; proclaimed defaulter on Stock Exchange; declared bankrupt and commercially exterminated
- **Collapse and Bitterness**: All ventures failed; came home announcing "We're ruined, Mary"; trembled and almost fell; aged visibly in six weeks more than previous fifteen years from creditor harassment; opened pent-up soul to wife, confessing losses, embarrassments, and treason of friends
- **Response to George-Amelia Affair**: When thinking of or alluding to affair between George and Amelia, spoke with bitterness almost matching Mr. Osborne's; cursed Osborne family as heartless, wicked, ungrateful; swore no power on earth would induce him to marry his daughter to Osborne's son; ordered Emmy to banish George and return all presents and letters

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; upon learning bankruptcy from husband, proved most faithful consoler; ran to him, kissed his trembling hand, poured out hundred words of incoherent love and tenderness; wrought his sad heart with inexpressible delight and anguish; cheering and solacing his overburdened soul
- **Current Status**: Living in reduced circumstances at St. Adelaide Villas with family

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; adored by men; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement Status**: Engagement to Amelia broken off by his father's veto; John Osborne menaced youth with maledictions if he broke commands
- **Status Change**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase (vice Smith)
- **Neglect and Debt**: Not visiting Amelia; seen at Opera by Edward Dale; won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards; father put instant veto on his intercourse with Amelia
- **Military Future**: Will form portion of British army now being mobilized against Napoleon

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; old friend and neighbor of John Sedley; George Osborne's father
- **Actions Against Sedley**: Most determined and obstinate opponent at creditor meetings; harassed Sedley severely; comported himself with savageness and scorn; almost succeeded in breaking bankrupt's heart; put instant veto on George's intercourse with Amelia; menaced youth with maledictions if he broke commands; vilipended Amelia as "basest and most artful of vixens"
- **Motivation Explored**: Under remarkable obligations to Sedley but subsequently quarreled; narrative reveals persecutor must tell and believe lies against hated object to remain consistent; from sense of consistency, must prove fallen man a wretch to justify own hard-heartedness, ingratitude, selfishness; thus Osborne required rupture of match to prove Sedley very bad character indeed
- **Servants**: Purchased port wine for Osborne's cellar from Sedley's sale

**Captain William Dobbin** [CHARACTER]
- Carried off George Osborne from billiards; served as agent bidding for small square piano at Russell Square auction; successfully outbid Rawdon's agent; acquired piano for Amelia Sedley's benefit
- **Character and Feelings**: Infatuated with Amelia (per family observations); blushed very much when jokingly asked if he would marry her; defended her passionately against Misses Dobbin's ridicule; said "Laugh and sneer at that angel. She can't hear it; and she's miserable and unfortunate, and deserves to be laughed at"; declared he would like to hear a man breathe word against her; corrected himself, calling women geese who hiss and shriek; threatened to become uproused British lion if anyone in barrack spoke against her; will form portion of British army now being mobilized against Napoleon
- **Family Opinions**: Mamma and sisters agreed his infatuation with "that silly little flirting, ogling thing" was never known; trembled lest, with engagement off, she take up Dobbin as other admirer; judged her according to their own notions of right and wrong

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Found marriage revelation letter on Rebecca's pincushion; read affecting document; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley; reported intelligence to Mrs. Bute
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; widower who proposed to Rebecca; broke out in fury upon learning marriage; ransacked her room at Queen's Crawley, destroying belongings
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; denies Rawdon and Rebecca access; returns letters unopened
- **Mr. Clapp**: Clerk of Mr. Sedley; found domicile with Sedley family at St. Adelaide Villas
- **Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Old servant; amassed considerable sum in service; staying with Sedley family at St. Adelaide Villas without wages; tends them and grumbles
- **Edward Dale**: Young stockbroker; saw George at Opera; member of Messrs. Dale, Spiggot, and Dale of Threadneedle Street
- **Islan Lindner, Dadette Lindner, Cotho Hollwood, Orbin Stenworth, Brevie Hollmere, Nynelle Hollmere, Fetho Hollmere, Lutho**: Secondary characters observing local rural events; Brevie Hollmere died quietly in sleep summer and buried at Salwick
- **Misses Dobbin**: Will Dobbin's mamma and sisters; ridiculed Amelia's engagement and folly; believed she would take up Dobbin if engagement with Osborne ended; now witness Dobbin's passionate defense of her

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **ENGAGEMENT RUPTURE**: John Osborne broke off match between Amelia and George; poor girl's happiness and character compromised; Osborne required strongest reasons for rupture and had to prove Sedley very bad character; father menaced George with maledictions if he broke commands; publicly vilipended Amelia as basest vixen; George placed under instant veto regarding Amelia
- **AMELIA'S HEARTBREAK AND ISOLATION**: Father ordered her to banish George and return all presents and letters; she promised but could not part with letters; brooded constantly over them; lived in past life; felt she would die or lose senses if torn from letters; looked to death with inexpressible longing; society now judges her as imprudent and criminal; reputation damaged; faces isolation and ridicule
- **SOCIAL JUDGMENT**: Misses Dobbin declare "Captain Osborne could not marry bankrupt's daughter"; Mrs. Smith and Mrs. Brown consider her criminal imprudence and horrid familiarities; peers judge her folly as passing all bounds; long engagement described as partnership where one party free to break while other invests all capital
- **NARRATIVE MORALITY**: Narrator warns young ladies: be cautious, wary of loving frankly, never tell all feelings, get married French way where lawyers are bridesmaids, never have feelings that make you uncomfortable or make unpromisable commitments; this is way to get on and be respected in Vanity Fair; narrator also notes obligation breeds enmity—persecutor must justify own ingratitude by proving fallen man wretched
- **MILITARY INTERVENTION**: French Emperor Napoleon's arrival in capital called up France in arms and all Europe to oust him; British army being mobilized for great chasse à l'aigle; Captain Dobbin and Captain Osborne form portion of this British military force; this military intervention will impact narrative
